subject: Clarify: model training exclusion and retention edge cases
messages:
From: Ethan Powell <epowell@novacorp.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Lee <sara.lee@novacorp.com>, security@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: model training exclusion and retention edge cases

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the intro yesterday. Our procurement and InfoSec teams are compiling a short risk package and need explicit answers around how Redwood treats customer content. Can you confirm the following in a short, shareable format?

1) Do you ever use customer-provided content (prompts, uploads, transcripts, or logs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update production models (including internal experiments)?
2) What are your retention timelines for: request logs, KV caches, debug snapshots, and backups? Do residual copies remain in cold archives or backups after a deletion request?
3) For dedicated or private deployments, how is data isolation enforced and who (if anyone) at Redwood can access raw customer transcripts?

We've attached our procurement questionnaire for reference. If you have a short SOC2/process document and a sample contract clause we can include, that would be very helpful.

Appreciate a concise bulleted response we can circulate to InfoSec.

Best,
Ethan
Security Operations | NovaCorp
Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Ethan Powell <epowell@novacorp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: model training exclusion and retention edge cases

Hi Ethan — thanks for laying this out clearly. High-level answers below (short version you can share with InfoSec):

• Training/use of customer content: We do not use customer content to train, fine-tune, or improve our shared production models. Customer data is not added to model training corpora as part of normal operations.

• Exceptions & troubleshooting: On rare occasions we may use a customer example for reproduction/debugging, but only with explicit customer consent and strict access controls; such instances are logged and scoped to a named ticket.

• Retention windows (defaults, can be contracted): request logs (90 days), KV caches/ephemeral session state (24–72 hours depending on session type), debug snapshots (kept up to 7 days before tombstone/purge), backups/cold archives (up to 180 days unless otherwise contracted).

• Private/Dedicated: For dedicated or private deployments, data is isolated at the tenant level; access to raw transcripts requires an internal role-based approval and is restricted to a small set of ops/engineering staff for emergency/debug only. Customers may request tighter controls or for us to disable certain debug artifacts.

• Evidence: Attaching a short SOC2 summary and our privacy addendum draft.

Next steps — I can: (a) share a tidy one-page response you can include in the package; (b) propose contract language for a non-training clause; or (c) hop on a brief call with your InfoSec to walk through the controls. Which would you prefer?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Ethan Powell <epowell@novacorp.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-20T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: model training exclusion and retention edge cases — technical detail

Ethan — adding a bit more technical color on the retention and deletion mechanics so InfoSec has specifics they can map to controls.

• Request logs: We retain request/usage logs for 90 days by default to support billing and incident investigation. Logs are indexed and immutable for that window, then moved to a purge queue.
• KV caches / session state: These are in-memory-first and written to ephemeral NVMe for very short windows; typical TTL is 24h. For streaming or long-running sessions the TTL can extend to 72h, but caches are never promoted to long-term training stores.
• Debug snapshots: When a reproduceable failure is captured we create a snapshot tied to the incident ID. Snapshots are TTL'd at 7 days by default; they are tombstoned and then purged by our background jobs.
• Backups & archives: System backups are lifecycle-managed; backup retention defaults to 180 days. After a deletion request we mark customer data as deleted (tombstone) in primary stores; the background workflow will remove objects from backups on their next rotation where feasible — we document limitations around immutable backups in our addendum.
• Audit & access: All access to customer raw transcripts requires an access request and is logged. Audit logs are retained 365 days. For Dedicated/Private customers we support shorter retention and options to disable debug snapshots or to provide end-to-end encryption with customer-managed keys.

If you need exact SLAs for purge timing or a playbook for legal holds, we can produce a one-off runbook for procurement.

— Priyom
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform

Dylan/Priyom — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups for procurement: 

1) Can you send a short contract paragraph we can drop into our vendor agreement that states Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or improve models (except with explicit, documented opt-in)? We want language that covers the backups/archives edge case.
2) Is there an API or portal endpoint customers can call to trigger deletion and see status?
3) Can you confirm whether debug snapshots and caches are included in the SOC2 scope / covered by encryption at rest?

If you can attach the sample clause and the privacy addendum we can circulate to legal. Also suggest a 30-minute call later today if available.

Ethan

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Ethan Powell <epowell@novacorp.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: model training exclusion and retention edge cases

Ethan — attaching a draft privacy addendum and a short sample clause you can paste into your MSAs. Quick answers inline:

• Sample clause: "Provider will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider's shared production models unless Customer provides explicit, documented consent for that purpose. Provider will not include Customer Data in model training corpora, and will exclude such data from any aggregate datasets used for model development." (See attached addendum for backup/archive caveat language.)
• Deletion API: Yes — customers can submit a deletion request via the Console or our DELETE /v1/customers/{id}/data endpoint. The request returns a job id and status you can poll; default purge workflows are invoked and tombstone/cleanup timing depends on backup rotation windows (see addendum).
• SOC2 / encryption: Debug snapshots and storage are within SOC2 scope; all customer data at rest is encrypted, and Dedicated/Private options can be configured with customer-managed keys.

Attachments: redwood-privacy-addendum.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute call (15:30 PT) to walk through this with your legal if that works.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
